newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks hit records as dollar surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks hit records as dollar surges.

text.p: The British and German stock markets surged through key index levels on Friday to record intraday highs, buoyed as the dollar hit a 30-month peak and Wall Street staged another record close.
Paris shares also hit an all-time high after a mixed start.
In London, the FTSE 100 stock index clambered above 4,200 points, propelled by another closing high for the Dow overnight and news that British interest rates were unchanged.
Not be outdone by its larger European rival, the Frankfurt bourse also climbed into uncharted territory as the German DAX index broke through the 3,000 threshold.
In London, investors heaved a sigh of relief after fears that Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke would raise interest rates to dampen inflation proved unfounded.

By 1100 GMT the FTSE 100 index of British blue-chip stocks was up 13.9 points at 4,211.4, surpassing the previous record of 4,198.9 set on Thursday when the market gained 38.6 points as it became clear that interest rates would stay put.

Dealers said a potential cloud on the horizon was political instability after Thursday's death of a Conservative member of parliament left Prime Minister John Major's government in a minority. But the chance of an early election was not having much impact on the FTSE, traders said.
Instead data on Thursday showing a fall in underlying British inflation in December and renewed talk of corporate merger activity also helped boost the FTSE.

"The market was certainly hyped up yesterday on hopes of merger and takeover possibilities," one trader said. "There's still a lot of cash around and while we are in this mood, people will be putting this cash into the market."
In Frankfurt, the DAX hovered around the 3,000 level and was at 3,001.38, up 8.07 points by late morning.

Dealers cited Wall Street, where after a roller-coaster ride the Dow Jones industrial average rose 38.49 points to a record 6,765.37 close, and the strong dollar. The mark, at its lowest level in years, was also good news for German exporters.
The dollar hit a 30-month high of 1.6038 marks in early trading, up from its late Thursday level of 1.5952/62.
It later slipped slightly, although it held above 1.60 and analysts saw little fundamental reason for dollar weakness.

"The dollar's come up a long way quite quickly, particularly against the mark, and I suspect we're due for a bit of profit-taking correction... But there isn't an awful lot standing in its way," said Robin Marshall, chief economist at Chase Investment Bank.
"The markets have got the view now that if they don't run into official resistance, they're just going to take it higher," Marshall said.

The market awaited U.S. trade data due at 1330 GMT and industrial output at 1500 GMT. If trade data for November shows the trade deficit is much bigger than expected, this could dampen the dollar, they said.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of a $9.8 billion deficit for the U.S. November trade balance.
Data for U.S. December industrial production, forecast on average to rise 0.6 percent after a 0.9 percent increase in November, will also be closely watched, analysts said.
The Paris bourse was more subdued, with prices mixed at the opening. But later the CAC-40 rose from Thursday's record close and was up 15.48 points at 2,423.25 at late morning.

Gold was firm in early European trading but dealers said it faced significant resistance at $355 an ounce amid bearish sentiment following news of a big sale of gold reserves by the Dutch central bank.
Gold started at $354.40/90 compared with Thursday's London close of $353.10/60.
Oil eased, with the Brent crude futures falling below $23 a barrel for the first time in more than a month.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 116.95 yen and 1.6035 marks, compared with 116.53 and 1.5945 late on Thursday.
Sterling firmed to 2.6810 marks from 2.6745 late on Thursday. The French franc eased to 3.3716 from 3.3748.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 15.5 points higher at 4,213.0, the first time it has gone through 4,200.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index broke through 3,000 and was up 8.07 points at 3,001.38 by late morning.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 13.42 at 2,421.19, also above Thursday's record close of 2,407.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $354.10, up from Thursday's afternoon fix of $353.05. Silver was slightly stronger at $4.76, up three cents from the previous London close.
